name: Zygomatic reduction

lead: Zygomatic reduction, also called malarplasty or cheekbone shaving, reshapes or repositions the cheekbones to give a narrower or flatter midface. People with a wide or prominent midface seek it for a slimmer facial width.

The cheek bone is cut and reshaped or moved inward, as forum posters describe it; some say shaving mainly reduces forward projection rather than width. On looksmax.org users debate whether width comes from bone or fat and whether the surgery improves proportions. The wiki's sources contain no outcome studies.

paras: It is a surgical procedure done under anaesthesia by a facial or plastic surgeon, popular in Asian aesthetic surgery. Swelling settles over weeks, and the final shape is judged after healing.
It is a bone-cutting operation under anaesthesia. Forum members report results ranging from very good to very bad, and no complication data were available in the sources used here.

angle.text: People with a wide or prominent midface want a narrower, slimmer facial width. The cheekbone is shaved or repositioned inward, so the change is visible after healing. Forum members report mixed before-and-after outcomes.

lead: Zygomatic reduction, also called malarplasty, cheekbone reduction or cheekbone shaving, is a surgical procedure intended to narrow or lower the projection of the cheekbones (the zygomatic bones). The zygomatic bone forms the cheekbone and part of the eye socket wall [1].

The procedure is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly by people with wide faces, with participants disagreeing about whether width comes from bone or fat and whether the surgery improves or harms facial proportions [2]. The material available for this entry is limited to a general anatomy reference and forum discussion.

paras: The zygomatic bone is a paired bone at the upper outer part of the face. It forms part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit and articulates with the frontal, sphenoid, temporal and maxillary bones [1]. Wikipedia notes that prominent cheekbones are considered attractive in some cultures and that some people undergo cheek augmentation, the opposite operation; it does not discuss cheekbone reduction [1].

lore.intro: A looksmax.org thread on cheekbone reduction shows the practice discussed as an option for wide faces, with disagreement about who benefits [2].

claims.claim: A wide face may come from bone rather than fat, and cheekbone reduction can improve it.
Cheekbone shaving mainly reduces forward projection, not width.
Surgery should only be done when the proportions truly call for it, since it can ruin a harmonious face.
